claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons have significant residual stress, a high defect density, and a nanoscale grain structure.
Residual deposition-induced strain and interfacial defects locally modify magnetic exchange parameters.
Residual strain and interfacial defects alter local magnetic-domain configurations.
Heterogeneous exchange interactions and deposition-induced defects enhance magnetic-domain pinning.
Enhanced magnetic-domain pinning widens magnetic hysteresis.
Strain- and defect-induced exchange heterogeneity reduces the peak magnetocaloric entropy change.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit a broadened magnetocaloric response and higher hysteresis under low-field cycling.
A mild inert-atmosphere anneal can relieve residual strain and reduce defect density without inducing phase segregation.
Annealing homogenizes magnetic exchange interactions and produces sharper, less hysteretic magnetic transitions.
After annealing, the maximum magnetic entropy change will increase toward bulk-like values relative to the as-deposited state.
After annealing, magnetic hysteresis will decrease relative to the as-deposited state.
Magnetic-entropy-change curves and magnetization-field loops can be used to evaluate magnetocaloric response and hysteresis, respectively.
The shape and peak magnitude of the magnetic-entropy-change curve affect magnetocaloric refrigeration performance.
Hysteretic losses can be important in magnetocaloric systems.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate in nanoscale films and nanoribbons where surface and interfacial effects dominate.
Heat-transfer rate limits the attainable cooling-cycle frequency and may continue to limit cooling after annealing.
The comparison should be performed at identical low applied fields and a fixed cycle frequency for annealed and untreated samples.

The strain-mediated hypothesis is falsified if annealing that demonstrably relieves strain does not significantly increase the magnetocaloric peak and reduce hysteresis relative to untreated controls.
Changes attributable primarily to annealing-induced phase segregation rather than strain relief do not support the proposed mechanism.
